claims.text: The materials under study are ferromagnetic materials.
SQUID magnetometry can determine the presence of ferromagnetic ground states at low temperatures.
Magnetic susceptibility is the structural mediator connecting SQUID magnetometry to identification of the ground state.
Magnetic susceptibility measurements provide the mechanism for detecting ferromagnetic ground states.
Applying SQUID magnetometry at low temperature will detect ferromagnetic ground states.
The baseline is the absence of ferromagnetic ground states.
Uncertainty limits the identification of ferromagnetic ground states.
Failure of SQUID magnetometry to detect a ferromagnetic ground state at low temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state labels the materials as ferromagnetic, while the baseline specifies absence of ferromagnetic ground states; without distinguishing finite-temperature ferromagnetism from a ferromagnetic ground state, these statements are in tension.
